structured_output.summary: The draining state is implemented end to end: enum, model and migration, scheduler, asset manager, public and UI APIs, CLI, docs and newsfragment, with tests at each layer. I ran all ten listed test files: 1 failure, `test_dag_command.py::test_cli_list_import_errors`, and everything else passes. That test asserts the worktree path appears in the log output, but the log shows `/work/tree/...`. It is a path mismatch in this environment, in code I didn't touch. I couldn't run ruff, prek or mypy in this session, so I kept lines short by hand; a ruff format pass is still needed. The migration and the model's `__table_args__` weren't checked against each other by a schema-sync test.

criteria_notes.note: `DagSchedulingState` added in `utils/state.py`. `test_state.py::test_dag_scheduling_state_members` checks the exact members and values.

`DagModel` has `is_draining`, a derived `scheduling_state` property and `set_scheduling_state`. In `test_dag.py`: `test_scheduling_state_derived_from_flags`, `test_set_scheduling_state`, `test_is_draining_defaults_to_false` and `test_db_rejects_paused_and_draining` (IntegrityError on both flags true).

Migration `0134_3_4_0_add_dag_is_draining.py` adds the column, the `idx_dag_is_draining` index, the check constraint and `idx_backfill_dag_id_completed_at`. `Backfill.__table_args__` declares the same index, and the `db.py` head map and `migrations-ref.rst` are updated. No test covers this beyond the model-level default and constraint tests above.

`dags_needing_dagruns` excludes draining Dags (`test_dag.py::test_dags_needing_dagruns_skips_draining`). Pending partitioned-asset events create no run for a draining Dag, and a run is created once it is active again (`test_scheduler_job.py::test_partitioned_dag_run_not_created_for_draining_dag`).

`test_manager.py::test_register_asset_change_skips_draining_dag` is parametrized over direct, alias, name-reference and URI-reference scheduling. It checks the event is recorded and only the active Dag is queued.

Task instances of a draining Dag are still queued (`test_scheduler_job.py::test_execute_task_instances_draining_dag_still_queues`). Its queued and running runs are still examined (`test_dagrun.py::test_draining_dag_runs_are_still_examined`). Manual triggers are not blocked: there is no code path to block them, and no test exercises one.

`_finalize_draining_dags` pauses idle draining Dags, clears draining and logs `drain_completed` with owner `scheduler` (`test_finalize_draining_dags_pauses_idle_dags`). It also pauses a Dag whose backfill has Dag runs (`..._waits_for_uninitialised_backfill`) or is completed (`..._ignores_completed_backfill`).

A Dag stays draining with a queued or running run (`test_finalize_draining_dags_waits_for_unfinished_run`) or a backfill with no Dag runs (`..._waits_for_uninitialised_backfill`). `..._orders_by_dag_id_with_limit_and_row_locks` checks dag_id order, the limit, and `skip_locked` with `of=DagModel` on the row lock.
`test_scheduler_loop_registers_finalize_draining_dags_every_5_seconds` runs the loop with a mocked `EventScheduler` and asserts `call_regular_interval(5.0, runner._finalize_draining_dags)`.
The auto-pause update in `dagrun.py` also sets `is_draining=False`. `test_dag.py::test_draining_dag_is_paused_and_not_draining_after_limit` covers it.

`DAGResponse` and `DAGDetailsResponse` carry `scheduling_state`, defaulting to `active`. `datamodels/test_dags.py::TestSchedulingState` covers the default. The public route tests `test_get_dag_reflects_draining` and `test_dag_details_reflects_draining` cover GET.

`DAGPatchBody` accepts exactly one non-null of `is_paused` and `scheduling_state`. `test_patch_dag_requires_exactly_one_field` expects 422 for both, neither, a null-only field and both null. `test_patch_dag_scheduling_state` includes the explicit-null cases.

`test_patch_dag_update_mask_must_match_body` and `test_patch_dags_update_mask_and_body_validation` cover the mask rules: a mask naming the other field gives 422, and an unsupported or double mask gives 400. `test_patch_dag_scheduling_state`, `test_patch_dag_is_paused_clears_draining` and `test_patch_dags_sets_both_flags` cover the response, clearing draining and the bulk PATCH setting both flags.
New `scheduling_state` filter on `/ui/dags`. `ui/test_dags.py::test_scheduling_state_filter` covers active, draining and paused, and checks that `paused=false` includes draining Dags.
`has_unfinished_runs` is computed for every listed Dag. `test_has_unfinished_runs_ignores_dag_runs_limit` puts the unfinished run outside the `dag_runs_limit=1` window and still expects true.

`set_is_paused` now uses `set_scheduling_state` and also matches draining Dags. `test_pause_unpause_change_draining_dag` covers pause and unpause. `test_cli_get_dag_details_includes_scheduling_state` covers `dags details`. I also added a `scheduling_state` key to `_get_dagbag_dag_details`, which the existing `test_dagbag_dag_col` requires.

A "Draining a Dag" section is added to `dags.rst` (plus a note under auto-pausing) and a FAQ entry to `faq.rst`. `newsfragments/22006.feature.rst` is added. I hand-edited the two OpenAPI yaml files; I did not regenerate them or check them with the generation tooling. The React UI, airflow-ctl and task-sdk clients are untouched.
